title: Scalar adjunctions and exact restrictions under coefficient equivalences
statement: Let $L:C\to D\dashv R$ and $L_0:C_0\to D_0\dashv R_0$ be adjunctions between arbitrary categories. Let $U:C\to C_0$ and $V:D\to D_0$ be equivalences and $k:UR\cong R_0V$ a specified natural isomorphism. There is a natural isomorphism $s:VL\cong L_0U$ such that $R_0(s_M)\,k_{LM}\,U(\eta_M)=\eta^0_{UM}$ for every $M$. In the pro-etale module categories of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], restriction along an isomorphism of coefficient ring sheaves is an equivalence on the unbounded derived categories. The restriction comparison for a commutative ring square is the composite of the two canonical scalar-restriction composition comparisons.

source.place: lemma-adjoint (07A6), scalar change specialization; Mathlib Adjunction/Mates iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv and unit_mateEquiv_symm

proof.text: The inverse ring map gives an inverse to scalar restriction. Compose the existing restriction composition comparisons with the identity-on-sections restriction identity. Exact localization transports the two inverse natural isomorphisms to the derived categories.

Take the inverse mate gamma of k. Mate gamma twice, the second time along U and V as equivalences. The second mate is invertible because its units, counits and k are invertible. The iterated-mates identity makes this the conjugate of gamma, hence gamma is invertible. Set s to its inverse and apply the unit equation for mates.

theorem scalarAdjunctionCoefficientEquivalence
    {C D C₀ D₀ : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category C₀] [Category D₀]
    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} {L₀ : C₀ ⥤ D₀} {R₀ : D₀ ⥤ C₀}
    (a : L ⊣ R) (a₀ : L₀ ⊣ R₀) (U : C ⥤ C₀) (V : D ⥤ D₀)
    [U.IsEquivalence] [V.IsEquivalence] (k : R ⋙ U ≅ V ⋙ R₀) :
    ∃ s : L ⋙ V ≅ U ⋙ L₀,
      ∀ M : C, U.map (a.unit.app M) ≫ k.hom.app (L.obj M) ≫
        R₀.map (s.hom.app M) = a₀.unit.app (U.obj M)
